PASSO 1: A ordem também muda: no genitiv: STEP 1: English has two ways to show possession: "Tom's car" and "the car of my father". German has both too, plus a third. With a proper name, the owner comes first and takes -s with NO apostrophe: «Toms Auto» (not Tom's). STEP 2: with an ordinary noun, the owner comes AFTER the thing, in the genitive — like English "of": «das Haus meines Vaters» (the house of my father), never «meines Vaters Haus». STEP 3: in everyday speech, «von» + dative works like "of": «das Auto von meinem Vater». STEP 4: one more trap: some masculine nouns take -n in every case except the nominative (der Student, den Studenten). English has nothing like this.
O português usa uma só palavra, “de”: “o: English uses 's and "of": "Tom's car", "the house of my parents", "the neighbor's car". German uses three paths: name + s («Toms Auto»), genitive after the noun («das Haus des Nachbarn»), or von + dative in speech («das Auto von Tom»).
PASSO 1: o GENITIVO responde a «wessen?»: STEP 1: the GENITIVE answers «wessen?» (whose?) and shows POSSESSION or belonging: «das Auto meines Vaters» (my father's car). STEP 2: the owner comes AFTER the thing owned — like English "of": «das Auto meines Vaters» = "the car of my father", not «meines Vaters Auto». STEP 3: genitive articles: masculine «des», feminine «der», neuter «des», plural «der»; indefinite: «eines», «einer», «eines». STEP 4: MASCULINE and NEUTER nouns add «-(e)s» — the same -s as English 's: «des Mannes», «des Kindes», «des Autos»; feminine and plural nouns don't change: «der Frau», «der Kinder». STEP 5: with PROPER NAMES, add «-s» with no apostrophe and no article, BEFORE the thing: «Annas Auto», «Pauls Buch». STEP 6: in speech, the genitive is often replaced by «von» + dative: «das Auto von meinem Vater».
o português usa «de» («o carro do meu pa: English 's and German genitive -s are the same old ending: "the man's" ~ «des Mannes». But German puts the owner after the noun with «des/der», and only proper names go in front («Annas Auto») — without an apostrophe.

Genitivo com adjetivos e em expressões d: The genitive with adjectives and in expressions of time and place
PASSO 1: com adjetivo, a terminação é «-: STEP 1: with an adjective, the ending is «-en» for all genders: «das Auto meines alten Vaters» (my old father's car), «die Tasche der netten Frau». STEP 2: the genitive appears in many EXPRESSIONS of time and place: «am Anfang des Jahres» (at the beginning of the year), «am Ende des Monats» (at the end of the month), «in der Mitte der Stadt» (in the middle of the city), «am Rand der Straße» (at the side of the road). STEP 3: with places: «die Hauptstadt des Landes» (the capital of the country), «die Größe des Zimmers» (the size of the room). STEP 4: «Name» and weak masculine nouns form the genitive with «-ns» and «-en»: «des Namens», «des Studenten».

PASSO 1: três preposições muito comuns p: STEP 1: three very common prepositions take the GENITIVE: «wegen» (because of), «während» (during) and «trotz» (despite, in spite of). STEP 2: «wegen des Wetters» (because of the weather), «während des Urlaubs» (during the vacation), «trotz des Regens» (despite the rain). STEP 3: with plural or feminine nouns, only the article changes: «wegen der Kinder», «während der Arbeit», «trotz der Verspätung». STEP 4: in conversation, many people use the DATIVE («wegen dem Wetter»); in writing and on exams, use the genitive. STEP 5: remember that «während» can also be a conjunction ("while": «Während ich arbeite, …»), and then the verb goes to the end.
Wegen dem Wetter bleiben wir hier.
Wegen des Wetters bleiben wir hier.
